feature1.prompt: Modify django/utils/autoreload.get_child_arguments to support autoreloading for non-Django modules. Currently, the function only detects when Python is launched with '-m django' by comparing file paths. The update must use Python's documented mechanism by inspecting __main__.__spec__ to determine if the -m option was used and to extract the package name. This change removes the restriction that prevents Django-based command-line utilities from using their own __main__ sub-module to override the built-in management commands such as runserver.
feature1.hint_texts: This part involves refactoring the implementation in django/utils/autoreload.py. Developers should remove the dependency on comparing __file__ from django.__main__ and instead import __main__ to check its __spec__ and __spec__.parent values. The new logic must add the '-m' flag with the correct package name when __main__.__spec__ is set, while preserving existing behavior for Django modules.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/utils/autoreload.py; Function: get_child_arguments; Focus on the code block around the detection of the -m option (lines ~216 and onward). Replace the current import of django.__main__ and the comparison with django.__main__.__file__ with a check on __main__.__spec__ and its parent.

tests.FAIL_TO_PASS: No new failing tests for Django module detection (existing tests for '-m django' should remain unaffected).
tests.PASS_TO_PASS: test_run_as_module, test_entrypoint_fallback, test_exe_fallback, test_raises_runtimeerror (from utils_tests.test_autoreload.TestChildArguments and related test classes)

feature2.prompt: Enable support for autoreloading when executing commands as non-Django modules. The goal is to allow commands like 'python -m pkg_other_than_django runserver' to work, thereby facilitating the creation of Django-based command-line utilities that use their own __main__ sub-module. This feature leverages Python’s documented approach using __main__.__spec__ to confirm that the -m flag was used and to capture the correct package name. Enabling this capability removes an impediment to overriding Django's built-in management commands with custom implementations.
feature2.hint_texts: This part focuses on updating the test suite so that the new behavior of get_child_arguments is properly verified for non-Django modules. Developers should add tests that simulate running the server with 'python -m' for a package other than Django. This includes creating a new test module to act as a non-Django __main__ and adding a test method (test_run_as_non_django_module) in tests/utils_tests/test_autoreload.py that asserts the correct child arguments are generated.
feature2.entrypoint: Files to modify: tests/utils_tests/test_autoreload.py (in the TestChildArguments class) and add the new file tests/utils_tests/test_module/__main__.py. The focus is on incorporating a test method that simulates non-Django module execution and verifies that get_child_arguments returns the expected argument list.

tests.PASS_TO_PASS: Existing tests that verify autoreload behavior for Django modules (ensuring they continue to pass)

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Files: django/utils/autoreload.py, tests/utils_tests/test_autoreload.py, tests/utils_tests/test_module/__main__.py; the get_child_arguments function and its related data structures.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 provides the updated implementation of the autoreload logic which Feature2's new tests are designed to validate. Both teams must ensure that changes made in get_child_arguments are correctly reflected in the test cases, so that autoreloading works seamlessly for both Django and non-Django modules.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature1 and Feature2 need to coordinate on the behavior of __main__.__spec__ detection and the expected argument list produced by get_child_arguments. Regular integration discussions are required to verify that modifications in the production code do not break the tests, and that any adjustments in logic are communicated and reflected in the test suite.
